g.text: Our map so far · M0–M1: Local-first core
New at this stop (pink): Desktop app, Markdown vault, SQLite/FTS5, graph — no AWS at all. Solid = already built · faded = still to come.
AWS Cloud · CHITKALA services account · one Region
Map so far: M0–M1 · Local-first core
The author works fully offline: the Markdown vault on disk
is canonical; editing, links, graph and FTS5 search never
If the author opts in, they sign in and the device is
The desktop calls the /v1 API with its JWT; AWS WAF
API Lambdas re-check every capability grant: the same
rules as the desktop's policy broker.
Tenant-scoped records (devices, grants, runs, audit index)
are keyed by tenant in DynamoDB.
Each tenant's data is encrypted with its own KMS key.
Key use is logged in CloudTrail; metrics and traces carry
correlation ids, never document bodies or prompts.
For a grounded question, the desktop retrieves locally and
sends only the scope-filtered context; the relay checks
Bedrock answers through Guardrails; the answer may cite
only the chunk ids it was given.
For the web companion, consented folders (and only those)
The indexer chunks by heading and asks Bedrock for
embeddings, recording the model and version.
Chunks, vectors, FTS fields and link edges are written to
Hosted questions use hybrid retrieval (vector + full text
+ graph) from Aurora before the model call.
A long-running or scheduled skill starts a Step Functions
agent run with its grants and budgets.
Planner and writer steps call Bedrock within the run's
Tools run in an isolated Fargate task: no internet, VPC
The run ends as a patch proposal pushed to the desktop
over WebSocket; the run waits for review.
The author reviews the diff; the desktop commits it
locally (compare-and-swap) and the run resumes. The cloud
To publish, only allowlisted, sanitized files are uploaded
An isolated CodeBuild project builds the Astro site and
runs the privacy, link and CSP checks.
After the author approves the preview, CloudFront switches
Readers get the public-only site, search index and graph.
